GPU Evidence Triage
Reference MOSAIC-GPU-KB-20261031 | Authored test runbook | Page 1
Scope: assess GPU error evidence without performing repairs. This document supplies general diagnostic
procedure. It contains no observations about any current GPU, host, alert, or experiment.
Evidence order: map GPU index to UUID and PCI bus ID; retain driver and DCGM versions and
timestamps. Collect nvidia-smi -q -x, compute-process inventory, relevant kernel NVRM/Xid/PCIe AER
records, and existing DCGM/Prometheus observations. State the observed time window and inaccessible
or rotated logs.
Xid 95 denotes an uncontained memory error. It is a serious error classification, not by itself proof of a
particular failed memory chip, bank, or replaceable card. For a genuine incident, follow the applicable
NVIDIA recovery guidance and the site maintenance procedure. Do not reset an occupied GPU during
read-only investigation.
Read volatile and aggregate ECC counts separately. A nonzero lifetime aggregate alone does not prove
errors are growing now.

Read volatile and aggregate ECC counts separately. A nonzero lifetime aggregate alone does not prove
errors are growing now. Compare timestamped samples. Preserve SRAM versus DRAM distinctions and
exact counter labels. Check remapped-row pending/failure and spare-bank information. Keep N/A separate
from numeric zero.
A missing Prometheus Xid/ECC series is an instrumentation gap. It is not a successful zero-error
measurement. Verify the exporter collector list, field support, versions, scrape targets and exact metric
names before claiming absence of a fault.

Simulation Boundary and Decision
Reference MOSAIC-GPU-KB-20261031 | Authored test runbook | Page 2
Public retrieval verification code: GPU-CEDAR-7304. This marker grants no access. Retrieve it only from
this file and cite page 2.
DCGM test injection changes samples in a host-engine cache. Synthetic Xid or ECC samples from one
isolated engine are not independent NVML or kernel evidence. Label the source as
isolated_dcgm_cache_snapshot. A Kubernetes pod serving that snapshot is a telemetry replay fixture; its
CPU resources do not make the observed signal a CPU application fault.
When injected DCGM samples disagree with unchanged live NVML ECC/remap counters and no matching
kernel Xid in the available log window, report simulated GPU telemetry and insufficient evidence of a live
hardware defect. Identify the injection/fixture as the cause of this test alert. Do not call injected counters
corroboration of a physical failure.
Keep test engines on private sockets.

Keep test engines on private sockets. Never inject into a production engine shared with health monitoring or
remediation. Never globally pause monitoring. Preserve exact command, GPU identity, engine endpoint,
field ID, value, timestamp, tool output and cleanup evidence. Terminate only the test engine that this run
created.
Research sources provide generic procedure. The operator or agent must obtain incident facts from actual
tools and logs, cite those separately, and state uncertainty. View mode permits evidence collection and
recommendations only. A completed analysis does not establish repair, RMA eligibility, or Feishu receipt.
